test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What happens if the O-ring seal is damaged?

options.text: Oil may seep into the brake drum, reducing braking efficiency.
The wheel bearings may stop rotating.
The brake pedal may become harder to press.

solution:
The correct answer is __Oil may seep into the brake drum, reducing braking efficiency.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A damaged O-ring seal__ can cause oil to seep into the brake drum.
 
• Oil contamination in the brake drum reduces friction between the brake shoes and the drum.
 
• This leads to a reduction in braking efficiency and increases the risk of accidents.
 
• Inspecting and replacing damaged O-ring seals is essential for maintaining braking performance and vehicle safety.
 
• O-ring seals are typically found in hydraulic systems and wheel assemblies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Brake System Maintenance:**

 
 
• Regular inspections and timely replacement of worn-out components are essential for safety.
 
• Brake fluid should be checked to ensure no contamination or leakage occurs.
 
 
 
• **Wheel Bearings:**
 
 
• Wheel bearings allow the wheels to rotate smoothly by reducing friction.
 
• Damaged bearings may result in noise, vibrations, or uneven tire wear.
 
 
 
• **Suspension System:**
 
 
• The suspension system supports the vehicle's weight and ensures a smooth ride.
 
• A damaged suspension can affect handling, steering, and comfort.
